content:
maria_support: FYI we just got a customer escalation — production app started seeing intermittent SSL handshake errors and 403s when using the Python SDK behind Gunicorn + Uvicorn. customer sees ~20% of requests failing, others ok. logs pasted below.

maria_support: customer env: Python 3.10, redwood-sdk 0.8.2, httpx 0.24.1, gunicorn 20.1.0 with --workers 4 --worker-class uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker, preload_app=True.

maria_support: log excerpt: 
```
ERROR httpx.RemoteProtocolError: TLS handshake failed: EOF occurred in violation of protocol (ssl.SSLEOFError)\n  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/httpx/_exceptions.py", line XX, in ...\n  File "/app/main.py", line 42, in make_call
  response = client.post(...)
```

maria_support: also seeing some 403s directly after a worker restart: `403 Forbidden` from our API with no body.

eng_liam: do they create a single SDK client at module import? that often hits post-fork issues with httpx and connection pools.

maria_support: yes they said they instantiate `redwood.Client(api_key=..., timeout=...)` at top-level and reuse across requests.

eng_liam: classic. if they preloaded the app then gunicorn forks after client created -> child workers inherit sockets/ssl state which can break TLS and pooled connections. leads to handshake failures and odd auth/no-crypto state.

eng_zoe: short repro steps we can give them: 1) disable preload_app (start gunicorn without --preload) 2) or move client creation into worker_process_init or app startup (use FastAPI lifespan). 3) quick workaround: re-create the httpx client in `on_startup` per worker.

maria_support: asked customer to try removing preload_app and restart one worker, will report back. they asked if there's an SDK-side mitigation so app-level changes not required.

eng_liam: SDK can guard against pre-fork reuse by lazily creating the underlying httpx client on first use and by exposing `close()` to clean up pools. but older 0.8.x may create Client eagerly. does 0.9.x change that?

eng_zoe: confirm: in 0.9.0 we switched to lazy transport init (created the async/httpx client on first request) and added a `Client.close()` that also closes pooled connections. recommend upgrading. also added docs about gunicorn preload.

maria_support: noted. customer can't upgrade immediately. any runtime workaround?

eng_liam: they can call `redwood.Client().close()` right after fork in worker_process_init, but we can't change their runtime easily. simplest is to create client inside `if __name__ == \"__main__\":` or in app startup. if using FastAPI: use `@app.on_event(\"startup\")` to set `app.state.redwood = redwood.Client(...)`.

maria_support: asked them to try creating client in startup and to paste new logs. also asked for `strace` or tcpdump? maybe overkill.

infra_bot: deploy-12345: restarted worker 2 on prod cluster (reason: config change).

maria_support: customer ran test after moving client to startup, failure rate dropped to <1%. they still saw occasional 403 after a burst.

eng_zoe: 403s after restart could be due to an auth race (token rotation) or our backend rate-limit/fallback returning 403 when TLS fails mid-handshake. ask for full request+response headers and exact SDK debug logs (`REDWOOD_HTTP_DEBUG=1` or enable httpx logging).

maria_support: requested debug logs and headers. customer provided this snippet: 
```
Request: POST /v1/generate Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\nUser-Agent: redwood-python/0.8.2 httpx/0.24.1\n
Response: 403 Forbidden\nX-Request-Id: abc123\nContent-Length: 0\n```

maria_support: no body, X-Request-Id present. forwarded to eng.

eng_liam: I checked logs for that request id on our side — we returned 403 because auth backend flagged malformed bearer header due to truncated bytes sometimes seen when TLS handshake aborted/retry mid-flight. so root cause still pre-fork client reuse or sudden connection resets.

eng_zoe: recommend: 1) short-term: set `retries=3` on the SDK's HTTP transport so transient TLS/EOF errors are retried. note: make retry idempotent only for safe endpoints. 2) medium-term: upgrade SDK to >=0.9.0 where lazy init + close is present. 3) strongly advise removing preload_app or re-initializing client after fork.

maria_support: will send patch notes and a step-by-step guide to customer: (a) disable preload_app, (b) move client init to startup, (c) add retries for transient network/TLS errors, (d) plan upgrade to 0.9.0.

maria_support: customer action items created and assigned. tagging eng to follow up on whether we should backport lazy-init/close to 0.8.x branch.

eng_liam: +1 on patch backport if it's small. can we add a log message when we detect post-fork reuse? helps ops.

eng_zoe: yeah we can add a `if os.getppid() != _CREATED_PID: logger.warn("Detected client created pre-fork; closing and reinitializing transport")` guard. low-risk patch.

maria_support: thanks all, will keep thread updated when customer confirms stable. :thumbsup:
